name: The Long March
traveler: The Central Red Army (the First Front Army of the Chinese Workers' and Peasants' Red Army)
summary: Encircled by the Nationalist armies, some 86,000 men and women of the Central Red Army break out of their base in Jiangxi and march for a year, about 10,000 kilometres, across eighteen mountain ranges and twenty-four rivers to the far north-west. At Zunyi Mao Zedong wins the leadership; at Luding they seize a chain bridge under fire; they cross snow mountains and the swamps of the grasslands. Fewer than eight thousand reach northern Shaanxi. The lands were long known; what the march made was a legend and a leader, and Edgar Snow's book carried it to the world.

stops.note: The army slips across the Yudu River at night and begins the march.
Running battle at the crossing of the Xiang; the army loses more than half its men.
The leaders debate where to go, and turn west into Guizhou.
The Zunyi Conference: Mao Zedong takes the leadership of the army.
Four crossings of the Chishui, doubling back to lose the pursuing armies.
Across the Jinsha, the upper Yangtze, in seven small boats over nine days.
Liu Bocheng swears brotherhood with the Yi chief Xiaoyedan, opening the way through Yi country.
Men cross the chains of the bridge under fire, its planks torn up, and take the Dadu River crossing.
Over the first of the snow mountains in summer clothes; many die of cold and thin air.
The army meets Zhang Guotao's Fourth Front Army.
A week across the swamps of Zoigê, where men sink into the bog and live on boiled leather.
The pass into Gansu, stormed up the cliff face.
Some eight thousand survivors reach the Red base in northern Shaanxi.
